messages:
alyssa: Hey team — customer (acme-prod) reports they got 403 when switching projects in the console after overnight IdP key rotation. Happens only in Chrome, Safari works. Can someone take a look?

kate: Thanks Alyssa. Do we have their org ID and a screenshot?

alyssa: Org: org_0xACME, project: project-dash-prod. Screenshot: 
`You do not have permission to view this project (403)`

mike: Any logs from the proxy? If it's after key rotation maybe session cookies are still valid but token introspection fails.

alyssa: I asked customer for a HAR but they sent a short curl repro: `curl -I -H "Cookie: session=eyJhbGci..." https://console.redwood.ai/api/projects/project-dash-prod` -> 403.

jordan: Could be the IdP rolled the signing key and our JWT verification fallback didn't pick up new JWKS quickly. Is there an auth-refresh job?

eng-bot: Deploy notice: idp-key-rotation job ran 2025-11-02T03:12:00Z across primary region.

mike: I pulled proxy logs for that org around 03:15Z — see snippet: 
```
[03:14:58Z] auth: token verified via cache, iss=https://okta.acme/idp
[03:15:03Z] auth: token signature invalid (kid mismatch)
[03:15:03Z] auth: lookup jwks cache -> stale, triggered refresh
[03:15:04Z] auth: jwks refresh success
[03:15:04Z] auth: token now valid
[03:15:04Z] proxy: accepted request
```
But some clients kept sending older cookies until browser session renewed.

kate: So that would return 200 once jwks refreshed. Why does customer still see 403 in Chrome?

jordan: Chrome may have pinned a stale cookie (our session cookie contains the original id_token fingerprint). If token signature check fails we drop to 403 rather than prompt reauth. That is by design for silent failures.

alyssa: Customer tried reload and still 403. They can workaround by signing out and signing back in. Asking for a less user-disruptive fix (we need to restore access without full sign-in if possible).

mike: Short term workaround: clear the site cookie for console.redwood.ai or open in incognito — reauth will issue fresh cookie. For automation we can offer them a curl pattern to exchange token: `POST /auth/reauth` with their current session cookie to get new cookie (but that's internal only).

jordan: For a longer-term fix we can add a graceful fallback: if signature fails but jwks refresh succeeds and the token is only a single-kid mismatch, attempt token revalidation path that allows short-window session refresh (issue new session cookie based on core idp SSO). Need eng approval.

kate: Customer is on a paid Dedicated plan — this is high priority. Alyssa, can you capture the user's session cookie (redact) + exact Chrome version and escalate to SRE with incident tag?

alyssa: Done — added ticket 2025-ACME-498 and attached the cookie, Chrome 117.0. Requested SRE escalation.

mike: I'll open an incident and set a temporary mitigator: make proxy return 401 (trigger client reauth) instead of 403 for signature-mismatch windows where jwks refresh completed within last 60s. That should prompt the browser to do a silent reauth flow instead of showing console error. Rolling a patch to staging now. @eng-bot can you create rollout?

eng-bot: Patch created: auth/fallback-reauth-60s. Rolling to canary 5% in prod.

kate: If canary looks good we can push to orgs affected. Alyssa — please inform customer of workaround (sign out / incognito) and that we're rolling a patch to prompt auto reauth which avoids full manual sign-in in many cases.

alyssa: Messaging sent — customer confirms incognito restored access. Leaving ticket open until patch validated. :thumbsup:
